patient._comment: 'patient' is info about the patient: personal, clinical, vitals are shown on the patient card during the game; diagnosis is used for potential 'patient review' card.

clinical.quoteLong: My breathing's been getting worse for two days — more wheezy, coughing up yellow stuff. I'm a longtime smoker with emphysema. My rescue inhaler barely helps now.
clinical.presentationShort: 66yo M with COPD ? 2 days worsening dyspnea, wheeze, and yellow sputum; accessory muscle use, inhaler barely helping, SpO2 88%.
clinical.presentationLong: 66-year-old male with COPD and two days of worsening breathlessness, wheeze, and increased yellow sputum. His rescue inhaler is barely helping; he uses accessory muscles, breathes 26/min, and has oxygen saturation 88%.

diagnosis.disposition: Acute → controlled O2 (target 88-92%), nebs, steroids, antibiotics, CXR; watch for CO2 retention.
diagnosis.why: COPD flare: nebs + steroids + antibiotics. Titrate O2 to 88-92% — too much oxygen can blunt the drive.

answer._comment: 'answer' is answer for the game scoring.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: leaning forward, hands on knees, pursed-lip breathing
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 66-year-old man, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: leaning forward with hands on his knees, pursed-lip breathing. Expression: tired and working to breathe. Clearly visible: a forward-leaning tripod posture and effortful breathing. No text, no logos.
